name: Array Stabilization (AND version)
description: You are given an array $$$a[0 \ldots n - 1] = [a_0, a_1, \ldots, a_{n - 1}]$$$ of zeroes and ones only. Note that in this problem, unlike the others, the array indexes are numbered from zero, not from one. In one step, the array $$$a$$$ is replaced by another array of length $$$n$$$ according to the following rules: First, a new array $$$a^{\rightarrow d}$$$ is defined as a cyclic shift of the array $$$a$$$ to the right by $$$d$$$ cells. The elements of this array can be defined as $$$a^{\rightarrow d}_i = a_{(i + n - d) \bmod n}$$$, where $$$(i + n - d) \bmod n$$$ is the remainder of integer division of $$$i + n - d$$$ by $$$n$$$. It means that the whole array $$$a^{\rightarrow d}$$$ can be represented as a sequence $$$$$$a^{\rightarrow d} = [a_{n - d}, a_{n - d + 1}, \ldots, a_{n - 1}, a_0, a_1, \ldots, a_{n - d - 1}]$$$$$$ Then each element of the array $$$a_i$$$ is replaced by $$$a_i \,\&\, a^{\rightarrow d}_i$$$, where $$$\&$$$ is a logical "AND" operator. For example, if $$$a = [0, 0, 1, 1]$$$ and $$$d = 1$$$, then $$$a^{\rightarrow d} = [1, 0, 0, 1]$$$ and the value of $$$a$$$ after the first step will be $$$[0 \,\&\, 1, 0 \,\&\, 0, 1 \,\&\, 0, 1 \,\&\, 1]$$$, that is $$$[0, 0, 0, 1]$$$. The process ends when the array stops changing. For a given array $$$a$$$, determine whether it will consist of only zeros at the end of the process. If yes, also find the number of steps the process will take before it finishes.
input_specification: The first line contains an integer $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \leq t \leq 1000$$$) — the number of test cases. The next $$$2t$$$ lines contain descriptions of the test cases. The first line of each test case description contains two integers: $$$n$$$ ($$$1 \le n \le 10^6$$$) — array size and $$$d$$$ ($$$1 \le d \le n$$$) — cyclic shift offset. The second line of the description contains $$$n$$$ space-separated integers $$$a_i$$$ ($$$0 \le a_i \le 1$$$) — elements of the array. It is guaranteed that the sum of $$$n$$$ over all test cases does not exceed $$$10^6$$$.
output_specification: Print $$$t$$$ lines, each line containing the answer to the corresponding test case. The answer to a test case should be a single integer — the number of steps after which the array will contain only zeros for the first time. If there are still elements equal to $$$1$$$ in the array after the end of the process, print -1 .
approach_summary: Formulate the state transition graph with non-negative weights. Execute Dijkstra's algorithm with priority queue to find shortest paths in O((V + E) log V).

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1579F — Array Stabilization (AND version) [168. Dijkstra's Algorithm]
topic_editorial.summary: Single-source shortest path using Dijkstra's algorithm.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: Because all edge weights are non-negative, the shortest distance to the unvisited vertex with the minimum tentative distance is finalized and cannot be decreased by further transitions (greedy choice property).
topic_editorial.solution_walkthrough:
### Step 1: Graph Modeling
Construct an adjacency list with pairs $(v, w)$ for each directed or undirected edge from $u$ to $v$ with weight $w \ge 0$.

### Step 2: Distance Table Initialization
Initialize $dist[v] = \infty$ for all vertices, with $dist[\text{source}] = 0$.
Push $(0, \text{source})$ into a min-priority queue `std::priority_queue<pair<long long, int>, vector<pair<long long, int>>, greater<>>`.

### Step 3: Relaxation Loop
While the priority queue is not empty:
1. Pop $(d, u)$. If $d > dist[u]$, discard (stale entry).
2. For each neighbor $(v, w)$ of $u$:
   If $dist[u] + w < dist[v]$:
   $$dist[v] = dist[u] + w$$
   Push $(dist[v], v)$ into the priority queue.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}((V + E) \log V)$
  Every vertex is extracted from the priority queue at most once. For every edge, we perform at most one priority queue push operation taking $\mathcal{O}(\log V)$.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(V + E)$
  Required for storing the adjacency list and the distance array.
